udt_struct_v0.doc:
Pool wiring and the currently active position range.

Everything here lives in a single **instance** storage entry. That is not a
style preference: the market-deposit path spans ReceiptVault -> this vault
-> the Aquarius pool -> three token contracts, and Soroban caps a
transaction at 100 footprint ledger entries. One entry per config field put
the end-to-end deposit at 113 and made it unexecutable on-chain.
udt_struct_v0.name: Config

udt_struct_v0.doc: Admin-tunable risk parameters. Also a single instance entry.
udt_struct_v0.name: Params

fields.doc: Cap on underlying deployed into the pool; 0 disables it.
fields.name: max_deploy

fields.doc:
Maximum tolerated gap between the pool's own swap quote and the
oracle-implied fair rate, in basis points. `0` disables the check.

The per-swap slippage floor is derived from `estimate_swap`, so it only
guards against movement between quote and execution \xe2\x80\x94 it cannot tell
that the pool itself is mispriced. Entering or exiting through a
dislocated pool can realize that gap immediately: on testnet a ~7%
pool/oracle divergence cost 4.65% of a deposit. This guards both
position entry and the paired-token leg of position exit.
fields.name: max_pool_divergence_bps

fields.doc:
How long a cached NAV root stays usable without re-reading the oracle.

This is a footprint budget decision as much as a freshness one: the
ReceiptVault withdraw path already spans six contracts, and pulling two
Reflector prices inside it pushed the transaction over Soroban's
100-entry cap. The ratio being cached is between two pegged assets, so
it moves slowly; `refresh_nav_root()` forces an update out of band.
fields.name: nav_root_max_age

fields.doc: Hard ceiling on how old the cached NAV root may be when the oracle is\nunreachable. Past this the vault refuses to price rather than serving an\narbitrarily obsolete ratio. `0` disables the bound.
fields.name: nav_root_max_stale

udt_struct_v0.doc: Keeper-managed range policy. Stored outside `Config` so an upgrade can\ndecode the exact Config value already present on Mainnet.
udt_struct_v0.name: RangeParams

fields.doc: Requested distance from the center to either edge, in raw ticks.\nBounds are rounded outward to the pool's tick spacing.
fields.name: half_width_ticks

fields.doc: Independent, tighter pool/oracle guard used only for recentering.
fields.name: max_rebalance_divergence_bps

fields.doc: Recenter when spot enters this many ticks of either edge.
fields.name: rebalance_margin_ticks

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Last observed token amounts backing the active concentrated position.

Unlike a full-range position, concentrated-liquidity NAV cannot be derived
from liquidity alone: its token mix changes as pool price moves through the
configured range. The keeper refreshes this snapshot from Aquarius and all
position mutations update it from actual token balance deltas.
udt_struct_v0.name: PositionAmounts

function_v0.doc: Conservative oracle-NAV quote; deposit pause is directional.
function_v0.name: quote

function_v0.doc: Deploys any idle underlying. Permissionless \xe2\x80\x94 it only ever moves the\nvault's own cash into the position it is configured for.
function_v0.name: deploy

function_v0.doc: Redeem shares for underlying. Thin wrapper so users are not forced to\nconstruct the DeFindex-shaped vectors.
function_v0.name: redeem

function_v0.doc:
Share balance. Read by `receipt-vault` through a SEP-41 `TokenClient`.

Renews the holder's TTL on the way past. `Shares(owner)` is persistent
state that is otherwise only bumped on write, so a market that holds a
position without depositing or withdrawing for the entry lifetime would
see its balance archived to zero while `total_shares` still counted it \xe2\x80\x94
and could then never redeem. `receipt-vault` reads this on every
boosted-value refresh, so renewing here keeps live claims alive.
function_v0.name: balance

function_v0.doc:
Accepts underlying and mints shares.

Deliberately does **not** call `from.require_auth()`: `receipt-vault`
pre-authorizes only the inner token transfer (contract.rs:311-327), and
that transfer's own auth requirement is what makes this safe \xe2\x80\x94 a caller
cannot pull funds from an address that has not signed.
function_v0.name: deposit

function_v0.doc:
Permissionless: claim the configured primary reward, third-party gauge
incentives and accrued swap fees, convert everything to underlying,
and redeploy.

Rate-limited because each call moves the share price; without a cooldown
it could be used to grind rounding in the depositor's favour.
function_v0.name: harvest

function_v0.doc: Transferable shares; registered custody moves preserve beneficial rewards.
function_v0.name: transfer

function_v0.doc: Burns shares and returns underlying.\n\nThe holder authorizes the exact withdrawal, including its output floor.
function_v0.name: withdraw

function_v0.doc:
Permissionlessly recenters the vault's one active position.

The old position is withdrawn in full. A single guarded swap converts
only the excess side into the exact token ratio quoted for the new
spacing-aligned range, avoiding a wasteful sell-and-buy round trip. The
call reverts atomically unless a new position is minted and at least
95% of the pre-deposit pair value is put back to work.
function_v0.name: rebalance

function_v0.doc:
Wires the vault to a concentrated Aquarius pool.

Pool metadata (tokens, decimals, tick spacing) is read from the pool
itself rather than passed in, so a typo cannot silently point the vault
at the wrong asset.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: Pauses new deposits. Withdrawals are deliberately never pausable: the\nmarket above must always be able to pull its cash back.
function_v0.name: set_paused

function_v0.doc: Permissionless bounded keepalive for the overlay's persistent records.
function_v0.name: stage_bump

function_v0.doc: Sells any configured reward held by the vault. Kept separate from\n`harvest` so a route can be exercised even when claiming is paused.
function_v0.name: sweep_reward

function_v0.doc: Total share supply.
function_v0.name: total_supply

function_v0.doc: SEP-41 spender authorization replaces the owner signature only; reward\ncheckpointing and all share/custody invariants use the same move routine.
function_v0.name: transfer_from

function_v0.doc:
Caps how much underlying may sit in the pool.

The realised APR of an LP position is the headline rate scaled by
`pool_tvl / (pool_tvl + deployed)`. On a thin pool an uncapped vault
dilutes itself to near-zero yield, so this is a yield control, not just
a risk control. `0` disables the cap.
function_v0.name: set_max_deploy

function_v0.doc:
Reconciles locally tracked liquidity against the pool's own view.

Permissionless: it can only ever replace the local number with the
pool's authoritative one, so there is nothing to gain from calling it.
function_v0.name: sync_liquidity

function_v0.doc: Permissionless TTL renewal for a share holder, for keepers that do not\nwant to pay for a full `balance` read path.
function_v0.name: bump_shares_ttl

function_v0.doc: Cheap simulation/read used by keepers to avoid submitting no-op\nrebalance transactions every polling cycle.
function_v0.name: needs_rebalance

function_v0.doc: Direct holder's unencumbered shares only. No swap or NAV dependency.
function_v0.name: emergency_redeem

function_v0.doc:
Forces a fresh oracle read of the NAV price ratio.

Permissionless, and the mirror of `receipt-vault`'s
`refresh_boosted_underlying`: keepers call it so user transactions get a
current value without paying the oracle's footprint cost themselves.
function_v0.name: refresh_nav_root

function_v0.doc:
Installs the actively managed concentrated-range policy.

Changing policy does not move funds. The permissionless keeper path
performs the migration only after its independent price guard passes.
This separation keeps governance changes reviewable and lets existing
Mainnet full-range deployments fail closed immediately after upgrade.
function_v0.name: set_range_policy

function_v0.doc:
Permanently binds the sole ReceiptVault allowed to deposit.

The candidate must already point back at this Aquarius vault and must
settle in the same underlying token. This closes both the supply-cap
bypass and an admin typo that would otherwise strand the deployment.
function_v0.name: set_receipt_vault

function_v0.doc: Read-only close quote. `min_swap` is the floor on the swap output of the paired\nleg only, which is what stage_convert_exit enforces. See ABI.md section 6.
function_v0.name: stage_quote_close

function_v0.doc: Single-sided deposit wrapper; the vault handles the paired asset split.
function_v0.name: deposit_underlying

function_v0.doc:
Sets the minimum raw underlying returned per raw reward unit, scaled by
`REWARD_RATE_SCALE` (1e7). A zero value removes the guard and therefore
disables selling that reward until governance installs a new floor.

The guard is intentionally independent of the route: changing a pool
must not silently weaken the fair-value floor. Keepers should alert and
leave rewards idle when a legitimate market move crosses the floor;
governance can then review and update it.
function_v0.name: set_reward_min_rate

function_v0.doc: Timestamp of the last successful oracle read. `0` means the cache has\nbeen invalidated and the next valuation must re-read the feed.
